clue.text: Composer of the Dargason ?

indicators.note: a composer puts notes in order, so whoever composes this tune's name reorders its letters

explanation.surface: A quiz question asking who wrote the folk dance tune Dargason.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dargason is an old English folk tune best known from Holst's St Paul's Suite, so Holst is the expected reply. Read 'Composer of' as the one who rearranges DARGASON, and the Spanish composer Enrique Granados appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrique Granados was a Spanish classical composer, and his surname is exactly the reshuffled letters of the tune's name.

clue.text: Lyrics included in version of " Hair " in Africa

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, as something included sits within it
a new version of a word is a different arrangement of its letters

parts.note: odes are lyric poems

explanation.surface: A rendition of the musical Hair, with its lyrics, staged somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of' rearranges the musical's title, and 'included in' puts the lyric poems inside it. The definition is the former name of present-day Zimbabwe, a land in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodesia was the colonial name of the southern African territory now called Zimbabwe (and Zambia, once Northern Rhodesia).

clue.text: The 7 lady's songsters

definitions.meaning: 7 down is LAMP, and the Lady with the Lamp was Florence, the Crimean War nurse; her surname with possessive 's
birds famed for their night-time song

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 7 down: 'The Lady with the Lamp' was Florence Nightingale, so 'The 7 lady's' is her surname with an apostrophe-s.
explanation.definitionFit: The nurse Florence's surname with possessive s sounds and spells the same as the plural of a famous singing bird.

clue.text: Pair of pistols 'e put in for this price

definitions.text: Pair of pistols 'e put in for this price

parts.words: Pair of pistols 'e put in for this price
parts.note: put an E into 'pistols' and you have pistoles, old Spanish gold coins; this Spanish gold coin was worth a pair of them

explanation.walkthrough: The pistole was an old Spanish gold coin, and this larger coin was worth two of them, so adding 'e to 'pistols' turns the gunfight into a price.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubloon was a Spanish gold coin, valued at two pistoles, so it is the price of a pair of them.

clue.text: Old Arab, TT perhaps, in the school sick-bay

indicators.note: the event is placed inside the sick-bay word

parts.note: SAN is short for sanatorium, the sick-room at a British boarding school
the TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle race, an example of a race

explanation.surface: An elderly Arab, perhaps a teetotaller, laid up in the school infirmary.
explanation.walkthrough: TT suggests teetotal, but here it is the Isle of Man TT motorcycle race. A SAN is the sick-bay at a British boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Saracen was the medieval European name for an Arab or Muslim, especially at the time of the Crusades.

clue.text: Alternative sort of lace delivered by Pythia

parts.note: OR introduces an alternative

indicators.note: a different sort of the word means its letters sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A different style of lacework handed over by the priestess Pythia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges LACE into ACLE. Pythia was the priestess at Delphi who spoke the god Apollo's prophecies.
explanation.definitionFit: Pythia was the prophetess at Delphi, and the prophetic pronouncements she gave were the Delphic responses known by this name.

clue.text: Illumination provided by many a current unit

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword stand-in for many
the amp is the unit of electric current

explanation.surface: Light supplied by many an electrical appliance running on current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many' is L, the Roman fifty; 'a current unit' is AMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp is a device giving light, so it provides illumination.

clue.text: Wise man in trouble with communications

indicators.note: the wise man sits inside the trouble word

parts.note: to be in a mess is to be in trouble
a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: A wise man finds himself in difficulty with his correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the wise man inside the trouble, after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Messages are things communicated, notes or words sent from one person to another.

clue.text: Barker of Yorkshire, first-class new leader

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as the letter I

indicators.note: a new form of the word means its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog from Yorkshire, top-class and recently made the pack leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' reshuffles the word leader, after A1 (with 1 as I). The breed is named after Airedale, the valley of the River Aire in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airedale is a large terrier breed from Yorkshire, and a barker is a dog.

clue.text: A sound introduction to various courses

definitions.text: A sound introduction to various courses

parts.words: A sound introduction to various courses
parts.note: the instrument struck to call people in to the several courses of a dinner, an introduction made by noise

explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' suggests education or racing; it means the courses of a meal, which a struck metal disc used to announce in grand houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner gong was struck to announce that the meal of several courses was ready.

clue.text: Whereby somebody can be brought to court

definitions.text: Whereby somebody can be brought to court

parts.words: Whereby somebody can be brought to court
parts.note: the writ requiring a detained person to be produced before a judge; the Latin means you should have the body, and 'somebody' splits as some body

explanation.walkthrough: The Latin writ means literally 'you shall have the body', hence the play on 'somebody'.
explanation.definitionFit: This legal writ orders a detained person to be brought before a court so the lawfulness of the detention can be tested.

clue.text: Sure, a true art form his, to satisfy the inner man

definitions.text: Sure, a true art form his, to satisfy the inner man

indicators.note: to form the words anew is to arrange their letters into a different shape

explanation.surface: Assuredly this person's genuine art is feeding hungry people well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' rearranges SURE A TRUE ART, and the whole clue also describes the person whose art is filling diners' stomachs.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurateur runs an eating house, whose trade is satisfying the appetites of hungry diners.

clue.text: A northerner makes smoke with one

indicators.note: one set of letters is made into another by rearranging them

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone from the far north lights up a smoke alongside one other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' rearranges SMOKE plus I (one); read the clue the other way, the answer's letters make SMOKE with I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inuit and related Arctic peoples were long called Eskimos, inhabitants of the far north.

clue.text: Plainchant, one supposes, in this office ?

definitions.text: Plainchant, one supposes, in this office ?

parts.words: Plainchant, one supposes, in this office ?
parts.note: split the name of the service into even and song, and 'even' means plain, so a plain chant; the office is a church service

explanation.walkthrough: 'office' is a church service, not a workplace. Splitting the service's name gives 'even song', and even suggests plain, hence 'plainchant, one supposes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening service, one of the daily offices, often sung.

clue.text: Falling behind with antifreeze precaution ?

definitions.meaning: trailing or dropping back behind others
insulating wrap put round water pipes so they do not freeze in winter

explanation.definitionFit: Lagging means trailing behind, and also the insulating material wrapped round pipes and tanks to stop them freezing.

clue.text: Hair stylist on the river

parts.note: a man in charge of locks, which can be tresses of hair or the gated chambers on a river

explanation.walkthrough: Locks are both hair and the gates on a canal or river, so the 'locks man' is no hairdresser but the keeper of a river lock.
explanation.definitionFit: A locksman is a lock-keeper, the person who operates a lock on a river or canal.

clue.text: Gets boat repaired in Spithead

indicators.note: something repaired is put back together, so the letters are reassembled in a new order

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of Spit

explanation.surface: Someone acquires a boat that has been fixed up at Spithead, the anchorage off Portsmouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repaired' reshuffles the boat. Spithead is a stretch of water off Portsmouth used as a naval anchorage; its 'head' here gives only the first letter of Spit.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to get hold of it, so obtains means gets.

clue.text: Cradle I found in a fish-trap

indicators.note: the letter is found sitting inside the trap words

parts.note: a bass is a fish and a net is a trap

explanation.surface: Someone discovers themself caught in a net for fish, like a baby in a crib.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts I between the fish and the trap; the hyphen in 'fish-trap' hides that they are two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A bassinet is a hooded wicker basket used as a cradle for a baby.

clue.text: Banks are in a reformed state

indicators.note: the letters are formed again into a new order

explanation.surface: The banking system is in a reformed condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' rearranges BANKS ARE; 'state' is a noun, a US state, not a condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebraska is one of the US states, in the Great Plains.

clue.text: He swears he's a mounted policeman in America

definitions.meaning: the idiom 'swear like a ...' makes this soldier a byword for bad language

definitions.text: he's a mounted policeman in America
definitions.meaning: a US state police officer, originally a mounted one

explanation.definitionFit: Troopers are proverbial for swearing, and in the United States a trooper is a state police officer.

clue.text: One who cares to drink a measure of the wine he keeps?

definitions.text: One who cares to drink a measure of the wine he keeps?

indicators.note: drinking takes the measure inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a carer is one who cares for someone
an ell is an old measure of length

explanation.surface: The keeper of a monastery's wine likes a sip of the stock he looks after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to drink' puts the old cloth measure inside the carer, after its first letter. The whole clue also describes the cellar officer who samples his stock.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellarer is the officer in a monastery or college in charge of the cellar and its wine and provisions.

clue.text: Newly drafted man on board — that's the end!

parts.note: the rook is a piece on a chessboard
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A fresh conscript on a ship exclaims that his career is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The board is a chessboard, not a ship: its piece is ROOK, then IE (that is). 'the end' reflects that IE comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookie is an inexperienced recruit, especially a new soldier, so a newly enlisted man.

clue.text: Attribute article to this writer

indicators.note: the article is added to the answer to make the first word, so it is taken off that word here

parts.note: to ascribe something is to attribute it
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Credit the newspaper piece to this author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attribute article to this writer' reads as ASCRIBE being A put to SCRIBE; take the article A away from ASCRIBE.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe is a writer, especially one who copied manuscripts by hand.

clue.text: Underground movements are in his sphere of study

definitions.text: Underground movements are in his sphere of study

parts.words: Underground movements are in his sphere of study
parts.note: not a resistance group but shifting of the earth below ground, studied by a scientist of earthquakes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Underground movements' suggests secret resistance groups; it means tremors in the earth's crust.
explanation.definitionFit: A seismologist is a scientist who studies earthquakes and the movement of the earth's crust.

clue.text: Bantu warriors in Blenheim picture

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: Zulu fighters depicted in a painting of the Battle of Blenheim.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'Blenheim' into 'picture'.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi is a Zulu or other Bantu regiment of warriors.

clue.text: Simple, or another of Marryat's seamen ?

definitions.meaning: Captain Marryat wrote Peter Simple and Mr Midshipman ..., two naval novels named after their young heroes

explanation.walkthrough: Frederick Marryat, a Royal Navy captain, wrote Peter Simple and Mr Midshipman Easy, so 'Simple' is also one of his seamen, and the answer is 'another'.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy means not difficult, and Jack Easy is the title hero of Marryat's Mr Midshipman Easy.

clue.text: Desire of a quiet little French girl

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
petite is the French feminine form of little, used for a small girl

explanation.surface: The wish of a soft-spoken small girl from France.
explanation.walkthrough: A, then P (piano, quiet), then PETITE, French for little in the feminine.
explanation.definitionFit: An appetite is a desire or craving, especially for food.

clue.text: Revolutionary club-man ?

parts.note: not a rebel but a member of a club whose name means turning like a wheel, a service club

explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests a rebel, but it puns on rotary, turning round; the club is Rotary International.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rotarian is a member of Rotary International, a club of business and professional people.
